oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: hosted-runtime kvcache OOMs detected in region us-west-2. automatic pager triggered for kvcache-prefetch growth.

oncall-bot: severity=P1, symptom=OOMs on inference workers, metric=kvcache.mem_used_pct, threshold=92%. Triggered at 2025-03-10T02:03:19Z.

jamal: seeing rapid upward slope on kv_map keys for session-type=chat-long. spike coincides with recent continuous-batching change (batch_window_ms=40 -> 80) rolled yesterday.

elaine: confirm: batch_window was increased for perf experiments last night? i thought we reverted?

mike: we rolled a config change to tune batching for short bursts, yes. the change bumped max_batch_latency to 80ms on hosted runtime pools A/B.

jamal: logs from one affected pod: ```
[2025-03-10T02:02:57Z] kvcache: insert_session id=abcd user_id=789 len=12800 kv_bytes=3.1GB total_keys=2.1M
[2025-03-10T02:03:02Z] runtime: OOM on alloc 1.2GB trying to allocate_kv_page
[2025-03-10T02:03:03Z] pod: evict_loop started, evicted 0 keys, mem_left 200MB
```

sara: customer-success ping: 3 customers reported timeouts: cust-omega, cust-redfish, cust-lighthouse. ETA on mitigation? customer-success will need a blameless note.

ops-bot: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) throttle prefetch depth to 1 for hosted runtime; 2) reduce batch_window_ms to 10 for affected pools; 3) enable aggressive eviction (evict_ratio=0.25).

jamal: i'm going to apply a hotfix patch to runtime config: disable prefix prefetch for requests with context_length > 4096, and set batch_window_ms=10 on canary. pushing now.

mike: tagging infra to give extra 8GB headroom to worker nodes in us-west-2 (small scale) while we stabilize. @infra-team please ack.

elaine: oncall: roll to 5% canary first and watch kv keys growth and mem_used_pct. I'll prepare the rollback if things degrade.

oncall-bot: DEPLOY START: 1765432205 - runtime-config-hotfix (jamal) -> pools: hosted-usw2-A, hosted-usw2-B (canary 5%).

jamal: canary applied. monitoring dashboards: grafana link https://grafana.redwood/boards/kvcache?org=1 (short link). watching mem_used_pct, kvcache.keys, batch_latency_p50.

(2m later)

jamal: canary shows immediate drop in kv_map growth rate, mem_used_pct down from 94% -> 76% on canary pods. eviction_count up slightly but stable.

elaine: good. start ramp to 25% for hosted-usw2 pools. incrementally update every 2m.

mike: infra increased node memory as a precaution, nodes back to green.

(5m later)

jamal: ramp to 25% complete. mem_used_pct trending down cluster-wide from 93% -> 69% after throttles + batch_window decrease. OOMs stopped.

customer-success: cust-omega reports degraded quality but service recovered. cust-redfish saw 20% request errors during the spike window. collecting logs for postmortem.

ops-bot: issued temporary rate-limit policy: requests with context_length>8192 are soft-throttled with 429 until further notice. applied at edge (gateway) and runtime.

sara: prepping customer comms: will notify impacted customers with timeline and mitigations. keeping message calm and technical.

elaine: decision: keep hotfix in place for next 24h while we run regression tests. create a follow-up ticket: KVCACHE-1279 to investigate continuous-batching regression and long-prompt behavior. assign to jamal + eng-ml.

jamal: capturing quick RCA notes: probable root cause = increased batch_window_ms expanded batching across long-prefix sessions, leading to larger aggregate KV prefetch windows and sustained KV mapping growth (prefix amplification). combined with long prompts (>=8k tokens) this pushed memory beyond eviction heuristics.

mike: action items:
- short: keep prefetch disabled for long contexts, maintain batch_window_ms=10 for hosted pools.
- medium: build detection to auto-reduce batch_window when kv_map growth rate > X.
- long: rework prefetch heuristics to be length-aware and cap per-session kv footprint.

ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2025-0310-KVCACHE-01, severity P1 -> linked to postmortem board.

jamal: handing off to night oncall (elaine) at 02:20Z. i'll be available for questions. leaving runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/kvcache-oom (appendix: rollout commands).

elaine: ack handoff. will monitor and hold cluster until 06:00Z. if mem_used_pct creeps above 85% again, escalate to pager.

customer-success: sending initial notice to impacted customers with ETA for postmortem (24-48h). will attach temporary mitigation steps and offer we can help re-route heavy sessions to dedicated capacity if they want.

jamal: small note — we should also examine the continuous-batching experiment metrics pipeline; there may be a test gap that let the 80ms change land without long-context simulation. adding test coverage.

elaine: closing update for now: root mitigation deployed, thermal OOMs ceased, customer impact contained to short window, next steps in INC ticket. will update status channel on any regressions. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, actions=hotfix-deployed, throttle-applied, canary-ramped, followup_ticket=KVCACHE-1279, handoff_owner=elaine.

mike: thanks all for quick triage. postmortem owners: jamal (tech), sara (comms), mike (infra).

elaine: logging timeline for postmortem: incident_start=1765432199, mitigated=1765432579, handoff=1765432619, closed_for_now=1765432799.

sara: will draft customer note and postmortem skeleton in #postmortems later today.

customer-success: confirmed customers received initial notice and appreciate the quick mitigation. will escalate only if we see recurrence.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (for now).
